'''Trevor Dion Wooley''' is a British mathematician, the Andris A. Zoltners Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at [[Purdue University]].<ref name="hovde">{{cite web |title=2024-25 Frederick L. Hovde Distinguished Lecturer |url=https://www.purdue.edu/science/hovde-distinguished-lecture-series/wooley-2024-25.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260421203017/https://www.purdue.edu/science/hovde-distinguished-lecture-series/wooley-2024-25.html |archive-date=2026-04-21 |access-date=2025-03-02 |publisher=Purdue University}}</ref>  His fields of interest include [[analytic number theory]], [[Diophantine equation]]s and Diophantine problems, [[harmonic analysis]],
the [[Hardy-Littlewood circle method]], and the theory and applications of exponential sums.  He has made significant breakthroughs on [[Waring's problem]], for which he was awarded the [[Salem Prize]] in 1998.

==Education and career==
Wooley read mathematics in [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]], receiving a [[bachelor's degree]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1987 with first class honours, and a master's degree in 1991.<ref name="cv">{{cite web |date=5 January 2025 |title=Curriculum vitae |url=https://www.math.purdue.edu/~twooley/20250105wooleycvbib.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211115547/https://www.math.purdue.edu/~twooley/20250105wooleycvbib.pdf |archive-date=2025-02-11 |access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> Meanwhile, he completed his PhD, supervised by [[Bob Vaughan]], in 1990 from [[Imperial College London]].<ref name=cv/><ref name=mg>{{MathGenealogy|id=7931}}</ref>

After postdoctoral research in the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], he became an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1991. He was promoted to associate professor in 1995, and full professor in 1998; he chaired the mathematics department from 2002 to 2005.<ref name=cv/>

In 2007 he returned to the UK as a professor of pure mathematics at the [[University of Bristol]], where he became head of pure mathematics from 2015 to 2016. At Bristol, his doctoral students included [[Thomas Bloom]].<ref name=mg/> He took his current position as Andris A. Zoltners Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at [[Purdue University]] in 2019.<ref name=cv/>

==Awards and honours==
Wooley was the recipient of the 1993 [[Berwick Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/LMSBerwick/|title=Winners of the Berwick Prizes of the LMS|work=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive|publisher=University of St Andrews|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> He was awarded the 1998 [[Salem Prize]] "for his work in [[additive number theory]], in particular on [[Waring problem|problems of Waring's type]]".<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|title=Wooley Awarded 1998 Salem Prize|date=December 1998|page=1483|department=Mathematics People|first=Jean|last=Bourgain|author-link=Jean Bourgain|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/199812/199812FullIssue.pdf}}</ref> He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM), held in [[Beijing]] in 2002,<ref name=icm>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=wooley|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|publisher=International Mathematical Union|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> and after receiving the 2012 [[Fröhlich Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/files/reports/LMS_Prizes_2012.pdf|title=LMS Prizes 2012|publisher=London Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> he spoke again at the 2014 ICM in [[Seoul]].<ref name=icm/>

He was elected as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2007,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/trevor-wooley-12565/|title=Professor Trevor Wooley FRS|work=Fellows Directory|publisher=Royal Society|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> and as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=1 September 2013}}</ref>
